Title: LSJ: Hunger Moon + Foul Blood interaction?

Messages.Author: OldFan
Messages.Body:
Hey Scott,

Just curious if it is possible for Hunger Moon and Foul Blood to
interact in such a way that a vamp with 1 blood on it goes to torpor?

Hunger Moon (Event)
----------------------------------
Transient.
Whenever a vampire successully hunts, move 1 blood from that vampire
to this card. Burn this card when it has five counters.

Foul Blood (Reaction/qui-QUI)
Cost: 1 blood
----------------------------------------------
Only usable when a vampire successfully hunts.
(qui) The acting vampire gains 1 less blood and takes 1 unpreventable
damage. Tap this reacting vampire.
(QUI) As above, but do not tap this reacting vampire.

My thought: A vamp with 1 blood declares a hunt action. No one
declares a block, thereby making the hunt "Successful". At this
point, Player B can ask Player A to move 1 blood (already on the vamp)
from Vamp A to Hunger Moon, and then plays Foul Blood, causing the
hunt to generate 1 less blood and inflict 1 damage, sending Vamp A to
torpor.

Or is this totally wrong? Can Player A, when Foul Blood is played:
1.) Hunt and move 1 blood on to Vamp A
2.) Move the just-gained blood to Hunger Moon
3.) claim that "the 1 less blood" provision doesn't work because the
blood is already gone (similar to a "burn 1 blood provision upon a
vampire with 0 blood on it)
4.) Take 1 damage, removing the blood counter it already had, leaving
it at 0 blood, but NOT in torpor.

Just confused how these 2 cards should interact.

Thanks!
-Asif Chaudhry

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
On Mar 28, 10:36 am, OldFan <asif.i.chaud...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hey Scott,
>
> Just curious if it is possible for Hunger Moon and Foul Blood to
> interact in such a way that a vamp with 1 blood on it goes to torpor?

No. Foul Blood is played before the vampire gains the blood form the
hunt (otherwise it could not modify the amount gained). Hunger Moon's
effect is applied after the vampire gains blood from the hunt.

A: Vampire Bob (with 1 blood) hunts (for 1).
Table: no block.
A: The hunt is successful (reaches for a blood from the bank)
B: Wait. Foul Blood. Bob gains 1 fewer blood from the hunt and takes 1
damage.
A: OK. The hunt is not successful* and Bob heals the damage (burning 1
blood).

Since the hunt is not successful, Hunger Moon's effect no longer
applies (although if it did, it would not have any effect, since Bob
has no blood to move to the event).

* http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/f280c5c520c84adc

> My thought:  A vamp with 1 blood declares a hunt action.  No one
> declares a block, thereby making the hunt "Successful".  At this

Making the action successful.

> point, Player B can ask Player A to move 1 blood (already on the vamp)
> from Vamp A to Hunger Moon, and then plays Foul Blood, causing the
> hunt to generate 1 less blood and inflict 1 damage, sending Vamp A to
> torpor.

B can't make A move blood to the event before A gains blood from the
hunt.

> Or is this totally wrong?  Can Player A, when Foul Blood is played:
> 1.) Hunt and move 1 blood on to Vamp A
> 2.) Move the just-gained blood to Hunger Moon
> 3.) claim that "the 1 less blood" provision doesn't work because the
> blood is already gone (similar to a "burn 1 blood provision upon a
> vampire with 0 blood on it)
> 4.) Take 1 damage, removing the blood counter it already had, leaving
> it at 0 blood, but NOT in torpor.

The "1 less blood" provision is not a retroactive effect. It isn't
that it is similar to burning blood on an empty vampire.
